wraps.note: This adapter describes and delegates to the CLI as it exists. It does not reimplement, patch, or replace any phase.

requirements.filesystem_note: Automatic shrink supports single-device Btrfs with optional LUKS. Automatic ext4 shrink is not implemented.

exit_codes.1: any failure: usage error, missing dependency, guard/refusal, or a phase that stopped before completing. The CLI has exactly two exit paths (`exit 0` and `exit 1` via its die() helper) and does not use distinct codes per failure class.

exit_code_notes: Exit codes were read from bin/usbless-dualboot and lib/*.sh: the union of explicit `exit N` statements is {0, 1}. Any claim of richer codes would be fabricated.

global_options.meaning: Machine-readable output on supported discovery commands
Print/check planned actions without disk or firmware writes

commands.name: probe
commands.summary: Detect disks, filesystems, encryption, bootloader, and firmware state.

json_output_schema.bootloader: string — free-form. Observed values: limine, systemd-boot, grub, unknown, and '<name> (inferred)' variants when it can only infer from a binary on PATH.
json_output_schema.lsblk: lsblk --bytes --json document; SIZE values are numeric bytes.

commands.name: guide
commands.summary: Print installer choices and recovery guidance for the saved plan.

commands.name: status
commands.summary: Report saved progress, recovery metadata and next steps.

commands.name: verify
commands.summary: Fingerprint a local ISO or compare its publisher SHA-256.

commands.name: doctor
commands.summary: Read-only readiness checks and actionable blockers.

commands.name: plan
commands.summary: Print a concrete, reviewable plan without changing anything.
writes: the config file at $USBDB_CONFIG only when --write is passed
commands.note: Default planning is read-only; --write saves a config and lock file. --json and --dry-run are not supported.

commands.name: shrink
commands.summary: Shrink the Linux partition/filesystem to free contiguous space.
writes: partition table of the target disk
the filesystem on the Linux partition
commands.why_dangerous: Rewrites the on-disk partition table and resizes a live root filesystem. It takes a partition-table backup and re-verifies disk size, disk GUID, partition start and PARTUUID before acting, and refuses on mismatch — but a successful shrink cannot be undone by the tool.
commands.guard: Checks planned identity/geometry, ISO fingerprint, single-device Btrfs minimum size/health, AC power and phase state; locks and backs up before changing storage.

commands.name: stage
commands.summary: Create the FAT32 installer partition, copy the ISO, and split install.wim if needed.
writes: partition table of the target disk
the ISO contents onto that partition
commands.why_dangerous: Creates a partition and formats it. Requires the shrink phase to have already completed and re-verifies the same disk identity guards.
commands.guard: Verifies planned identity, ISO fingerprint, kernel geometry and free installer range; locks and backs up before writes. A prior shrink is unnecessary if the range is already free.

commands.name: boot
commands.summary: Register a one-time UEFI boot entry for the installer, or restore boot order.
writes: UEFI NVRAM boot variables via efibootmgr
commands.why_dangerous: Mutates firmware NVRAM rather than disk contents. --restore reverses the boot-order change, which is why this is classed firmware rather than destructive.

commands.name: windows
commands.summary: Add or remove a Windows entry in the boot menu for the detected bootloader.
writes: ESP bootloader configuration (limine.conf, loader/loader.conf, or grub.cfg)
commands.why_dangerous: Edits the boot menu on the EFI system partition. It copies the existing config to a timestamped .bak before changing it, so the edit is reversible.
commands.guard: Requires the Windows EFI binary to exist at $ESP_MOUNT/EFI/Microsoft/Boot/bootmgfw.efi.

commands.name: secureboot
commands.summary: Sign the Linux boot chain with sbctl and guide key enrollment.
commands.why_dangerous: Key enrollment writes to firmware key stores and is the phase that can make a machine unbootable if it is abandoned half-way, which is why the CLI splits it into --prep, --enroll and --verify and requires Setup Mode.
commands.guard: Modes are --prep, --enroll, --verify; enrollment requires Setup Mode to be enabled.

danger_scale.boot-config: Writes bootloader configuration on the ESP. Backed up first, so reversible.
danger_scale.firmware: Writes UEFI NVRAM or firmware key stores. Reversible with care, but affects bootability.
danger_scale.destructive: Alters the partition table and/or filesystem contents. Cannot be undone by the tool.

implemented: Argument passthrough to the real bash CLI.
A machine-readable command manifest (this file) exposed via `manifest --json`.
Danger-class reporting and a root precheck before delegating.
No phase is reimplemented in Python.
not_implemented: REPL / stateful multi-operation sessions. The underlying CLI is a set of one-shot phases driven by a state directory, so there is no persistent interactive session to expose.
Undo/redo. The bash CLI has no undo stack; shrink and stage are irreversible, so claiming undo would be false.
The adapter delegates CLI commands only. The separate native Qt app provides graphical previews.
not_verified: No mutating phase (shrink, stage, boot, windows, secureboot) has been executed or end-to-end tested, here or by the adapter's author: it would require real block devices and root.
The registry entry has not been submitted to HKUDS/CLI-Anything; no upstream maintainer has reviewed or merged it.
This adapter has not been reviewed or adopted by CLI-Anything; `cli-hub install usbless-dualboot` does not work until the upstream registry entry is merged.
